inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash-flow statement SBC add-back $69.0M (SEC XBRL via Metrics.csv). No combined SBC-plus-withholding figure is published; withholding taxes on net-share settlement are immaterial (<$15M/yr) and not added.
inputs.share_count_basis: Q2 2026 10-Q diluted weighted-average shares 144.6M (quarter ended 2026-06-30). Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows. STLD is a heavy repurchaser ($900.9M FY2025, $315.4M H1 2026, ~$261M disclosed around Q3 2026), so the flat count is funded, not a convention; Q3 2026 repurchases (~1.2M shares) are not yet in a filed count and are left out (conservative by <1%).
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Risk-free ~4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, levered beta ~1.3 (US EAF steel, cyclical) -> cost of equity ~10.7%; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.3% (senior notes), ~4.1% after tax; debt ~11% of EV at market -> WACC ~10.0%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality is priced in the scenario flows and the beta, not in an ad-hoc premium (adaptations 7f).
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP: operating-lease cost already sits inside EBITDA (treatment B). total_debt is senior notes/borrowings per the Q2 2026 balance sheet; operating-lease liabilities are not in net debt. Leases are small for STLD.
inputs.nci_treatment: Noncontrolling interests are immaterial (single-digit $M share of net income in recent years); flows are consolidated with no NCI deduction.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, mid-cycle treatment (routing row: cyclical US operating company -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md). Steel is a spread business: EBITDA margin has run from ~0% (2009) to 25% (2021-22) to 11.2% (FY2025); the 10-year (FY2016-25) average is 16.4%. Neither FY2025's trough margin + growth-capex FCF ($432.5M owner FCF) nor the 2026 tariff-boosted run-rate is capitalised; FY2026 is built off guidance (H1 actual revenue $11.3B, EBITDA $1.57B; Q3 EPS guide $5.34-5.38), and margins revert to a mid-cycle level from FY2028. FY0 is FY2025; the growth path compounds from FY2025 revenue $18,176.6M. Interest income not stripped: STLD is net debt ($3.6B at 2026-06-30), not net cash. Capex follows management's framework (H2 2026 $300-350M, FY2027 up to $500-600M, sustaining $250-300M thereafter) for the first three years, then rises to D&A by the terminal year because a 2.5% nominal perpetuity on a ~$27B revenue base cannot be held on a $300M sustaining budget. Working capital: manufacturer with inventory + receivables well above payables, so capture is NEGATIVE (-20% of revenue change; H1 2026 OCF of $576M against $1.57B EBITDA is exactly that drain). Cap multiple 12x (cyclical): Gordon at 10%/2.5% is 13.7x, so the cap binds in base/bull. Net debt from Q2 2026 10-Q; Q3 2026 results (due 2026-10-19) will refresh it.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: mid-cycle judgment, not a trailing CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Every trailing CAGR is a cycle-position artefact. 5-year windows start at the FY2020 COVID trough (revenue +13.6%, EPS +25.2%, equity +16.4%); 3-year windows start at the FY2022 peak (revenue -6.5%, EPS -27.5%, owner FCF -50.1%). Equity 5yr (16.4%) diverges >30% from revenue 5yr and from all 3yr rates. FY2020 owner FCF was negative (-$266.6M, Sinton capex), so the 5yr FCF CAGR is undefined.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF = reported FCF - SBC (no interest-income strip; net debt throughout). Owner-FCF CAGR (-50.1% 3yr) is below reported FCF CAGR (-48.5%) only marginally: SBC is ~0.4% of revenue, so the gap is capex (Sinton, Columbus aluminum, satellite slab centres) and spread compression, not stock comp. Selected 3.0% is a long-run nominal volume + price rate for US steel/aluminum with Columbus ramping to 650kt.

base.narrative: FY2026 lands near guidance (~$23.4B revenue, ~16% EBITDA with Q3 the peak quarter); FY2027 holds on fabrication backlog and aluminum volume, then steel prices normalise from FY2028 as tariff support fades or imports adjust; aluminum reaches profitability and lifts the mid-cycle margin to 16%, in line with the FY2016-25 average.

bull.narrative: Section 232 at 50% is extended beyond December 2027 and reshoring/data-centre demand keeps US spreads structurally wider; Columbus fills its 650kt on auto and can-stock contracts and reaches its targeted ~$650-700M EBITDA by 2028; the margin settles at 18%, the level STLD earned in 2018 plus a profitable aluminum leg.

bear.narrative: Tariffs are rolled back or negotiated away when the regime lapses in December 2027 while new US EAF capacity (Nucor, CMC, Big River 2, Nippon-US Steel) floods flat-rolled; HRC spreads compress to FY2024-25 levels and a US industrial/construction slowdown hits fabrication; Columbus ramps late and sub-scale against Novelis, keeping the mid-cycle margin at 13%, below the decade average.

scenario_narratives.base: Mid-cycle. FY2026 is the guided up-leg (record shipments, Q3 EPS guide $5.34-5.38, tariff-supported spreads) and is not capitalised: revenue eases ~4% in FY2028 as steel prices normalise, while Columbus aluminum moves from ramp losses to profit and the fabrication backlog (+45% YoY into Q1 2027) carries FY2027. The long-run EBITDA margin of 16% equals the FY2016-25 average, which already includes the 2021-22 super-cycle and the 2019-20 and 2024-25 troughs. Capex follows management's step-down ($500-600M FY2027, then sustaining) before rising to D&A as the asset base ages.
scenario_narratives.bull: The axes break STLD's way: Section 232 protection outlives its December 2027 sunset, US reshoring and data-centre construction keep domestic steel demand and spreads above the last decade's average, and the Columbus aluminum mill (650kt, recycled-content can stock and auto sheet) proves the steel playbook transfers, adding a ~$650-700M EBITDA leg. Margin 18% through the cycle, growth 3% long run.
scenario_narratives.bear: The axes break against it: tariff support is withdrawn at the 2027 sunset and imports return, the wave of new domestic EAF flat-rolled capacity drives a price war, and a US industrial slowdown hits auto, construction and fabrication at once. Columbus stays loss-making longer against entrenched rollers (the 2026 satellite-slab relocation and $16M impairment are the warning). Mid-cycle margin 13%, two years of revenue decline, higher capex intensity relative to a shrunken revenue base.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25% (up from the 15% default): the stock is priced on an up-cycle quarter inside a tariff regime with a dated sunset, and the bear axis (spread compression plus new domestic EAF supply) is a recurring feature of this industry, not a tail. Base 50%: mid-cycle reversion is the historical norm. Bull 25% (down from 35%): it needs tariffs to persist AND the aluminum ramp to hit target AND spreads to stay above average, three largely independent conditions.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Steel Dynamics is valued on a mid-cycle owner-FCF basis: the current guided up-leg is modelled explicitly for FY2026-27 but never capitalised, and the terminal year carries the decade-average 16% EBITDA margin with capex at D&A. Cyclicality is priced in the scenario flows and a beta-built 10% WACC, once. The terminal value is capped at 12x owner FCF (~7x EBITDA), a normal US steel multiple.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cycle position: today's price embeds the tariff-supported 2026 spread; a single year of FY2024-25 margins on the current revenue base removes ~$1.5B of EBITDA
Section 232 sunset (December 2027) is a binary policy input the model treats as a gradual normalisation
Columbus aluminum ramp: the base case assumes it reaches profitability by FY2028; slippage keeps a loss-making segment inside a 16% consolidated margin
Capex: management's $250-300M sustaining figure is well below D&A (~$700M); the model rises to D&A by the terminal year, and holding to management's figure would add materially to value
Working capital: price-driven revenue swings move inventory and receivables by ~20% of the revenue change, so the FY2026 up-leg absorbs ~$1B of cash
